case_name: Sri.Ramappa vs The Secretary on 8 June, 2026

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: SRI. RAMAPPA, S/O SIDDAPPA, AGED ABOUT 64 YEARS
parties.respondent_defendant: THE SECRETARY, MINISTRY TO REVENUE DEPARTMENT, KARNATAKA GOVERNMENT OF KARANTAKA

facts_of_case: Petitioner claims to be the husband of Gangamma, whereas respondent No.5 denies that he is not the husband. There was no marriage between Gangamma as the petitioner was the husband of one Lakshmidevi and not Gangamma.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnized after the commencement of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 shall be null and void if it contravenes any one of the conditions specified in clause (i), (iv) and (v) of Section 5.
legal_principles.held: Section 11 of the Act declares such a marriage as null and void in the following terms: Any marriage solemnized after the commencement of this Act shall be null and void and may, on a petition presented by either party thereto against the other party, be so declared by a decree of nullity if it contravenes any one of the conditions specified in clauses (i), (iv) and (v) of Section 5.
cited_cases: Yamunabai Anantrao Adhav Vs. Anantrao Shivram Adhav and Another, (1988) 1 SCC 530

legal_principles.principle: No aid can be taken of the earlier Hindu law or any custom or usage as a part of that law inconsistent with any provision of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
legal_principles.held: By reason of the overriding effect of the Act as mentioned in Section 4, no aid can be taken of the earlier Hindu law or any custom or usage as a part of that law inconsistent with any provision of the Act.
cited_cases: Yamunabai Anantrao Adhav Vs. Anantrao Shivram Adhav and Another, (1988) 1 SCC 530
